study_type_evidence.quote: Mice were acclimatized for 1 week and intravenously injected with 200 μL of Atto647N-labeled CCPMs in PBS (5 μg/μL) or PBS (control) through the tail vein.
The nanoparticles (30 g/L) were incubated with EDTA-stabilized, pure, and undiluted plasma (1:1, v/v) at 37 °C for 1 h.
The samples were measured in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) buffer at 25 °C and at a detection angle of 173°

in_vivo_species.quote: Male C57Bl/6 mice, aged 13–17 weeks, were housed in individually ventilated cages under a constant condition with a 12 h light–dark cycle

ex_vivo_detail: Human blood plasma pooled from six healthy donors (EDTA-stabilised, obtained from the transfusion centre of the Medical Department of Johannes Gutenberg-University Mainz) was incubated 1:1 (v/v) with nanoparticles at 37 °C for 1 h and analysed by AF4 and FCS - a stability/aggregation assay on blood taken out of the body, hence ex vivo. Separately, mouse organs (lungs, liver, spleen, kidneys, heart, small intestine) were excised 72 h post-injection and imaged ex vivo on an IVIS Spectrum (animal-origin ex vivo work).
in_vitro_detail: Particle characterisation in buffer only: DLS in PBS, FCS in PBS/water, HFIP-GPC; no cell culture experiments reported.

concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Nanoparticle circulation time analysis was calculated from the nanoparticle fluorescence in blood plasma samples. Normalization to 10 min time point, fit model: monoexponential decay (B).
concentration_time_figure.note: Plasma nanoparticle-associated fluorescence (% of the 10 min value) plotted against time; blood sampled at 10 min, 1 h, 6 h, 24 h and 72 h after i.v. dosing. Half-lives derived by monoexponential fit.

bioanalytical_method: Fluorescence quantification of the Atto647N label in plasma using a Tecan Spark plate reader (ex 640 nm / em 670 nm); ex vivo organ biodistribution by IVIS Spectrum fluorescence imaging.
bioanalytical_quote: The particle fluorescence was quantified by a Tecan Spark plate reader (Tecan Group Ltd.) at an emission wavelength of 640 nm and a detection wavelength of 670 nm
notes: In vivo PK was run only for the three CL30-series particles (NCL30, 2F-CL30, 3F-CL30); the CL17 series and PM30 were characterised only in buffer and human plasma, so Table 1 leaves their t1/2 cells blank. The authors state the differences in half-life were not significant and that normalisation to the 10 min timepoint may have missed an early drop. The permitted animal-work reference is AVD1060020187085 (Leiden University). No Cmax/Tmax were computed because data were normalised to the 10 min value rather than reported as absolute concentrations.
